diagnosis.summary: A traffic surge and DynamoDB read throttling on the product-service table are active at the same time, affecting all four services. Product-service p95 latency is at 3196 ms against a baseline of 6.56 ms and its 5xx error rate is 1.56% against a baseline of 0. The incident has been running for approximately 2 minutes.
diagnosis.root_cause: A traffic surge across all four services and DynamoDB read throttling on the product-service table, active at the same time, are the most likely root cause.
evidence: Request rate rose on all four services: product-service from 14.98 to 27.87 rps (86% increase), cart-service from 2.05 to 6.15 rps (~3x), order-service from 2.97 to 8.83 rps (~3x), and payment-service from 0.94 to 4.55 rps (~4.8x).
Product-service read throttle events are at 7031/min and throttled requests at 5223/min, both up from a baseline of 0.
Product-service db_latency_ms_p95 rose from 5.61 ms to 3196 ms, approximately 570x the baseline.
Product-service p95_latency_ms rose from 6.56 ms to 3196 ms, approximately a 487x increase from baseline.
Product-service error_rate_5xx is at 1.56%, up from a baseline of 0.
Product-service lambda_duration_ms_mean rose from 2.49 ms to 7.49 ms, approximately a 3x increase from baseline.
recommended_actions: Increase read capacity on the product-service DynamoDB table immediately to reduce the 7031 read throttle events/min and restore p95 latency and error rate; this is the fault with the most direct user impact.
Set rate and burst limits on the API Gateway stage to cap the traffic surge and prevent further pressure on all services while the throttling fault is being addressed.
Check Lambda concurrency across all four services to confirm the shared account concurrency limit is not being exhausted given the broad request rate increase.
Review product-service Lambda logs for timeout and retry patterns during the throttling window to understand the error volume.

After increasing DynamoDB capacity, recheck all signals including request_rate, read_throttle_events, db_latency_ms_p95, and error_rate_5xx to confirm each fault has cleared before making further changes.
